title: Safety and immunogenicity of an inactivated thimerosal-free influenza vaccine in infants and children.
ehr_evidence: Data were collected prospectively through scheduled clinical visits, parent-completed adverse event diary cards, and blood samples assessed by hemagglutination inhibition and single radial hemolysis assays in a phase III clinical trial (NCT00700193).
summary: A prospective, open-label, phase III clinical trial evaluating the safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity of a thimerosal-free inactivated influenza vaccine (Fluvax/C210) in 298 healthy Australian children aged 6 months to <9 years.
key_findings: No withdrawals occurred due to adverse events, and the majority of solicited local and systemic adverse events were of mild severity.
Severe injection site pain and fever were reported by only 3.0% and 3.4% of participants, respectively.
The vaccine was immunogenic for all antigens, with ≥95% of both younger and older children achieving seroprotection after dose 2.
No significant difference in baseline seropositivity to any vaccine antigen was found between children who reported prior influenza-like illness and those who did not.
An unexpected discrepancy between HI and SRH assay results for the influenza B strain was observed following the booster dose in Group A.
captured_features: solicited local adverse events (erythema, swelling, pain)
solicited systemic adverse events (fever, irritability, cough, rhinitis, loss of appetite, myalgia, sore throat, vomiting/diarrhea, wheezing)
unsolicited adverse events and serious adverse events
study_design: prospective, open-label, phase III clinical trial
population: 298 healthy children aged 6 months to <9 years (Group A: ≥6 months to <3 years; Group B: ≥3 years to <9 years) at two Australian pediatric hospitals
limitations: Lack of a placebo control group; all participants acted as their own controls.
Open-label design with first occurrences of solicited local adverse events arbitrarily deemed related to the vaccine.
Different influenza B strains between the 2005 and 2006 seasons limited comparability of booster responses.
No group comparison inferential statistics were applied.
